source.title: Reward value-based gain control: divisive normalization in parietal cortex.

confidence_rationale: This entry supports SD-082's PRINCIPLE and undercuts its FORM. Support: Louie et al. show that neurons in monkey lateral intraparietal cortex do not encode the absolute value of an option but a relative value 'explicitly dependent on the values of the other available alternatives', including alternatives outside the response field, and that this context-dependence is 'precisely described by divisive normalization'. So the general architectural commitment SD-082 makes -- that a per-candidate quantity feeding choice should be computed relative to the rest of the candidate set rather than absolutely -- is how a real decision circuit works, not a convenience. This matters because SD-082's centering is otherwise open to the objection that it discards information the agent might need. Undercut: the measured cortical operation is DIVISIVE gain control (scale by a denominator summing the alternatives' values), not SUBTRACTIVE mean removal. These have different consequences under exactly the regime SD-082 operates in. Divisive normalization rescales a near-collinear set without changing its poor angular separation, whereas subtraction removes the shared offset and amplifies the residual -- so the paper's mechanism would NOT have repaired the V3-EXQ-822 structural zero, and the paper is therefore evidence for context-relative coding in general and against the claim that SD-082's specific arithmetic is the biologically attested one. Confidence 0.61: strong primate electrophysiology, but the form mismatch is central rather than peripheral to what SD-082 asserts, and the area is LIP rather than lateral PFC.
failure_signatures: FORM MISMATCH, and it is not cosmetic. Divisive normalization scales a set of values by a common denominator; subtractive centering removes a common addend. Under the SD-008 regime these come apart decisively: dividing a set of near-collinear vectors (min cosine 0.963) by a scalar leaves them just as collinear, so a divisive read-out would have reproduced the V3-EXQ-822 structural zero, while subtraction is what rescues it. SD-082 therefore cannot claim divisive normalization as its biological warrant. If SD-082's architecture doc or claims.yaml entry is ever read as 'normalization is canonical in cortex, therefore SD-082 is biologically grounded', that inference is invalid -- the canonical cortical operation is the one that would NOT have worked here.

Louie et al.'s normalization is over the values of concurrently available ALTERNATIVES and is reported in baseline firing rates as well as stimulus-driven activity, i.e. it is a persistent property of the circuit. SD-082's centering is gated on K >= 2 candidates and computed per tick with no memory. A single-candidate tick therefore receives no centering at all, so the read-out's input statistics change discontinuously with candidate-set size. Nothing in this paper (or in SD-082's validation plan) tests whether that discontinuity matters, and a mixed-K episode could show tick-to-tick bias instability that the window-mean prop_delta would average away.

OPEN DISAGREEMENT WITH A SIBLING ENTRY IN THIS SAME DIRECTORY, recorded rather than resolved. The earlier entry 2026-07-29_sd_082_divisive_normalization_canonical_carandini2012 (landed REE_assembly e41e28d6f3) reads normalization as supporting BOTH SD-082 components at once, on the ground that normalization 'discounts the pooled common drive AND bounds the response smoothly'. This entry argues the discounting half does not transfer, because divisive scaling of a near-collinear set does not improve its angular separation. Both are partly right and the reconciliation is a real refinement: divisive normalization DOES fix the SATURATION half (dividing by a denominator that pools the alternatives pulls an over-driven set back into dynamic range, which is exactly the clamp-rail problem) but does NOT improve the SIGNAL-TO-COMMON-MODE RATIO (for summaries x_i = c + delta_i with c >> delta, division returns (c + delta_i)/(sigma + Kc), preserving the small relative differences instead of exposing them). Subtraction addresses both halves; division addresses one. So SD-082(i)'s subtractive choice is better-motivated than the Carandini entry implies and better-motivated than pure form-mismatch would suggest -- but the biological attestation covers only the weaker operation. Governance should not treat either sibling entry as settling this; the discriminating measurement is REE-side (the angle between the common mode and the candidate-discriminative direction), not literature-side.

The paper's headline behavioural consequence of normalization is IRRATIONALITY -- context-dependent violations of rational choice, where the presence of a third option changes the preference between two others. If SD-082's centering imports the same context-dependence into the candidate bias, then the bias becomes a function of which other candidates happen to be in the set on that tick. That is arguably correct as biology and is a hazard for any REE claim that treats the bias as a stable per-candidate property. It should be checked before SD-082's centering is inherited by consumers beyond the SD-078 path.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Neurons in monkey lateral intraparietal cortex encode a relative form of saccadic value that is explicitly dependent on the values of the other available alternatives, including target values outside the neuron's response field, and is visible in baseline firing rates as well as stimulus-driven activity. This context-dependent modulation is precisely described by divisive normalization -- the same gain-control form seen in extra-classical receptive-field effects in visual cortex -- suggesting normalization is a general mechanism of cortical computation. In decision circuits it implements an adaptive gain control for value coding and provides a mechanistic basis for behavioural context-dependent violations of rationality.
mapping.ree_translation: The transferable content is the PRINCIPLE that a per-alternative quantity driving choice is computed relative to the concurrently available set, not absolutely -- which is the general commitment behind SD-082(i)'s decision to condition the lateral-PFC bias head on the candidate set rather than on each candidate in isolation. Louie et al. establish that a real primate decision circuit does this, which answers the objection that set-relative conditioning is an engineering convenience that discards information. What does NOT transfer is the arithmetic. SD-082 subtracts the across-candidate mean; LIP divides by a denominator pooling the alternatives. Applied to REE's actual problem the two diverge: division cannot repair a near-collinear candidate set (it rescales without separating), so the biologically attested form is the one that would have left prop_delta at 0.0. SD-082's subtractive choice is warranted by the ML precedent (dueling networks) and by the population-geometry premise (Kaufman et al.), not by this paper.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Three boundaries, the first of which is the point of the entry. (1) FORM: divisive is not subtractive, and in the SD-008 collinear-cone regime the difference decides whether the read-out is repaired -- so this paper must not be cited as biological warrant for SD-082's mechanism, only for its motivating principle. (2) AREA: LIP saccadic value coding, not lateral PFC rule-to-action read-out; SD-082's subject is a prefrontal analog, and normalization's generality across cortex is argued in the paper rather than demonstrated for PFC. (3) QUANTITY: the normalized variable is a reward value driving saccade selection, whereas SD-082's centered variable is a z_world candidate summary -- an encoder latent, not a value. The transfer assumes the set-relative principle is indifferent to whether the per-alternative quantity is a value or a representational summary, which is plausible but untested.
mapping.source_context: Primate electrophysiology. Single-unit recordings from lateral intraparietal cortex in macaques performing value-guided saccadic choice with varied reward magnitudes across two or more targets, with target values manipulated both inside and outside the recorded neuron's response field. Divisive normalization fitted quantitatively against alternative models of context dependence.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality 0.87: J Neurosci, primate single-unit recordings, the normalization model fitted quantitatively rather than asserted qualitatively, and the result has been extended and replicated by the same group (Louie, Khaw & Glimcher 2013, PNAS, doi 10.1073/pnas.1217854110, extends it to choice behaviour in monkeys and humans; Louie 2022, PLoS Comput Biol, doi 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010350, to asymmetric reward coding in RL). Mapping fidelity 0.50, the lowest in this pull and deliberately so: the paper evidences set-relative coding, which SD-082 does assert, while the specific operation it attests to is the one that would NOT have fixed the V3-EXQ-822 zero. A design_decision claim lives or dies on its mechanism, so a form mismatch at the mechanism is a halving, not a rounding. Transfer risk 0.50: LIP to a lateral-PFC analog, and reward value to encoder latent, are both substantive leaps; normalization's claimed cortical generality mitigates but does not remove them. Aggregate 0.61, direction mixed -- this is the entry that keeps the pull honest, by recording that the canonical cortical normalization is divisive and that SD-082's subtractive choice therefore rests on its ML precedent rather than on this biology.
